label: MVC: classify each item
prompt: Click M, V, or C to assign each snippet to its layer. Each one belongs clearly to one part of the Model-View-Controller pattern.

items.explanation: Querying the database is the Model's job — it owns all data access and business rules.
Rendering data as markup is the View's responsibility — it only displays, never decides what to show.
Handling a route and deciding what to do next is the Controller's job — it's the mediator between View and Model.
Business rules and data validation live in the Model, not the controller or view.
The form is part of the interface the user sees and interacts with — that's the View, even though it triggers an action.
Deciding where to send the user based on application state is control flow — squarely the Controller's territory.
